title: Auditor Briefing: Access Model 2 & Event Export Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is an auditor-facing briefing + internal checklist covering our Access Model 2 (next-gen role model for serving and control plane), the audit log schema we export to SIEM, and the automation/evidence slices we plan to hand to SOC 2 / ISO 27001 auditors. Use this during auditor walkthroughs and for last-minute evidence grabs.

Audience:
- External auditors (SOC 2/ISO)
- Internal reviewers (security, SRE, platform eng)
- Solutions engineering for customer-facing questions

High-level summary (one-pager):
- What we’ll show: role lifecycle (create/assign/revoke), enforcement points (API gateway, authz proxy, runtime enforcer), audit log events for every access decision, corresponding SIEM export with context, and end-to-end evidence retrieval automation for a 90-day window.
- Primary controls mapped: SOC 2 CC6.1 (access provisioning), CC6.8 (least privilege), CC7.3 (log collection), ISO 27001 A.9 (access control), A.12 (logging), A.18 (audit and compliance).

Access Model 2 (short explainer):
- Terming: we avoided "RBAC v2" in consumer docs and use "Access Model 2 / AM2" internally to emphasize scoped roles + attribute-based scoping.
- Components: Roles (name + immutable role-id), Grants (role -> resource pattern), Principal binding (user/service account -> role, with expiry), Session token (short TTL + session attributes), Enforcement (policy engine at edge + runtime fallback).
- Key guarantees auditors ask about: role auditability, deterministic revocation, time-bounded bindings, and separation of duties for role management APIs.

What an auditor typically asks (and our canned answer):
Q: How do you prove a role was revoked before an access event?
A: Show binding revocation event (am2.binding.revoke), then show downstream evaluation that returned DENY for subsequent request. Export contains both events with same binding_id and correlated request_id.

Q: Can you show who created a role and its approver?
A: Yes — am2.role.create and am2.role.approval events include creator_id, approver_id (if approval workflow used), role_definition_hash, and a Git reference when role was created via IaC (repo+commit).

Audit log schema (fields we persist and export):
- timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
- event_type (string; e.g., am2.binding.create, authz.evaluation, session.issued)
- event_id (ULID)
- request_id (ULID; propagates across services)
- principal_id (user|service:<id>)
- principal_type (user|service|machine)
- role_id (if applicable)
- binding_id (if applicable)
- resource (ARN-like pattern)
- action (api-method or permission string)
- decision (ALLOW|DENY|ERROR)
- decision_reason (short string; e.g., expired_binding, explicit_deny, missing_role)
- policy_version (string)
- token_id (opaque; for session correlation)
- src_ip
- user_agent
- service (which Redwood service emitted the event)
- raw_payload_snippet (base64 JSON up to 4KB)
- retention_label (e.g., prod-sensitive, long-term)

Note: We include a small raw_payload_snippet for quick triage; full event JSON is stored in coldstore for forensic export.

SIEM export formats and handshake:
- Primary push: JSON-lines (newline delimited JSON) over secure SFTP for scheduled batches (hourly) to customer's SIEM ingestion bucket.
- Real-time: HTTPS POST to our SIEM forwarder which supports CEF and Elastic Common Schema (ECS) mapping.
- Export envelope includes minimal PII and references full-event ids for auditor retrieval (do not rely on exported json_lines as sole evidence).

Evidence automation and retrieval flow (for auditor requests):
1) Auditor requests: provide time range, sample principal_id or role_id, and required controls.
2) Run automated evidence job (evidence-service/job-run) that assembles a zip with: filtered event JSONL, timeline.csv (human readable ordered events), IaC refs, role definitions, binding metadata, and a signed manifest (SHA256).
3) Manifest contains provenance: job_id, requester, checksum per artifact, and retention window.
4) Delivery: pre-signed secure URL or direct SFTP drop.

Gap analysis summary (top issues remaining):
- G1: "Decision_reason" length sometimes exceeds SIEM field limits (we currently truncate to 256 chars) — mitigation: normalize reasons to canonical codes; ETA Q2 2026.
- G2: Not all legacy service token events propagate request_id consistently — mitigation: retrofit instrumenters with middleware; ETA Q1 2026.
- G3: Selected bindings created via tooling lacked approver metadata when created via the legacy admin UI — mitigation: deprecate old UI and backfill approvals via event-sourcing job; ETA Q1 2026.
- G4: Some export batches missed src_ip due to older proxies dropping X-Forwarded-For — mitigation: ensure global edge inserts client_ip header; ETA immediate (done for new regions).

Checklist for auditor demo (quick run):
- Pre-reqs: Confirm auditor has temporary SFTP creds and NDA-signed evidence request.
- Step 1: Pull list of role_ids for target product team (roles.csv). Query: SELECT role_id, name, created_at, created_by FROM am2.roles WHERE team='serving-runtime';
- Step 2: Evidence job: evidence-service/run?from=2026-01-15T00:00Z&to=2026-01-31T23:59Z&filter=principal_id:U-12345
- Step 3: Show correlated events: am2.binding.revoke -> authz.evaluation (DENY) -> session.invalidate. Provide request_ids for each.
- Step 4: Export manifest and signed checksums; demonstrate artifact verification (sha256sum).

Sample auditor queries (Kibana/Elastic & SQL-like):
- Kibana (ECS): event_type:"authz.evaluation" AND decision:"DENY" AND principal_id:"user:U-12345" | sort @timestamp asc | show request_id, decision_reason, role_id
- Elastic PPL: source = "am2" | where event_type=="am2.binding.revoke" and binding_id=="B-6789" | fields @timestamp, request_id, principal_id
- SQL-like (internal): SELECT timestamp, event_type, request_id, decision, decision_reason FROM audit_events WHERE principal_id='user:U-12345' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-01-10' AND '2026-01-20' ORDER BY timestamp ASC;

Evidence retention & legal considerations:
- Default retention: 90 days hot (searchable), 2 years cold (on object storage w/ encryption), 7 years archived per legal hold on request.
- Exported artifact TTL: evidence job produces signed package with one-time pre-signed URL valid 14 days unless auditor requests extension.
- Redaction policy: PII redaction is applied on exported artifacts unless explicit written consent requested in audit scope. See policy ref: confluence:SEC-219-redaction-policy.

Operational runbook snippets (for SRE on call):
- If auditor reports missing events: verify request_id correlation across services (span sampler), check message queue retention for event-topic (currently 7 days), and re-run event backfill job.
- If exported JSON lines fail SIEM ingestion: run the JSON-L int job (tools/validate-jsonl) and repackage with ECS mapping.

Unresolved discussion items (for next security sync):
- U1: Standardize decision_reason to an enum set (list needed from product). Who owns? Product-Auth.
- U2: Decide if coldstore full events are encrypted with customer-specific KEK for private deployments (privacy requirement vs operational complexity).

Appendix A — Example event (single-line JSON preview):
{ "timestamp":"2026-01-18T14:12:11Z", "event_type":"authz.evaluation", "event_id":"01F7Z9X0Q1RM2Z6A9B2K3C4D5E", "request_id":"01F7Z9WRMJS1A4B6C8D0E1F2G3", "principal_id":"user:U-12345", "role_id":"R-serve-core", "resource":"/models/da-v2/predict", "action":"invoke:predict", "decision":"DENY", "decision_reason":"binding_expired", "service":"inference-gateway", "src_ip":"3.94.15.22" }

Appendix B — Suggested artifacts to attach for typical SOC2 walk:
- roles.csv (export of am2.roles)
- bindings.csv (export of am2.bindings with active/expired flags)
- sample evidence job package (zip) with manifest and sha256s
- IaC refs for role definitions (repo+commit link)
- screenshots of admin UI audit trail for role changes (if requested)

Who to contact for each area:
- Access model questions: Nina Alvarez (nina@redwood.com)
- Audit log schema & SIEM export: Samir Desai (samir@redwood.com)
- Evidence automation & delivery: June Park (june@redwood.com)
- Legal/retention: Theo Martinez (theo@redwood.com)

Notes to self / meeting prep bullets:
- Bring pre-built evidence job for demo (test job id: evjob-20260118-42).
- Confirm auditor SFTP IP whitelist ahead of time.
- Have a backup: if SFTP blocked, give access via ephemeral workspace in secure review bucket.
